newsitem.title: USA: Mixed noon dlr eyes US Tsy slump from new mark top.
newsitem.headline: Mixed noon dlr eyes US Tsy slump from new mark top.

text.p: Dollar/yen had erased early gains by midday but after wavering on a strong report from the nations purchasers, dollar/mark ignored tumbling U.S. Treasuries and powered to a new 93-month high, dealers said.

"The question becomes: 'Does the dollar continue to make gains on the interest rate expectations scenario or does the dollar top out and sell off on the broad U.S. asset market selloff here,'" asked Bob Near, a vice president of corporate foreign exchange at Bank of New York.
At noon, the dollar fell to 118.37/42 yen from 119.00/05 at the open but surged to 1.8620/30 marks from 1.8530/34.
The dollar got a big boost against the mark in early New York trade after a startlingly strong July U.S. jobs report contained no sign of upward pressure on wages.
But dollar/yen and dollar/mark decoupled early on, when large sales of mark/yen cut off the dollar's overnight rally to 11-week highs over 119 yen.

Later in the morning, a 1-1/2 point plunge in Treasuries and a 100-point plus drop in the Dow industrials following the National Association of Purchasing Management's July report briefly deflected dollar/mark, before its relentless rally carried it to the highest level since November 1989.
"The nervousness in U.S. asset prices has kicked in, as well as the mark/yen selling that has driven dollar/yen down," said Seth Garrett, chief dealer at Credit Suisse First Boston.
The NAPM index for July rose to 58.6 compared to 55.7 previously and forecasts of 56.1. The prices index, widely watched by investors, jumped to 53.6 from 48.1 in June.
The price component, though worrisome, contrasted with a flat average hourly earnings reading in the July jobs data.
The unemployment rate returned to 4.8 percent, lowest in nearly a quarter century, and the non-farm payrolls figure rose a startling 316,000.

"I don't think the numbers today change what the (Federal Reserve) is going to do anytime soon but they certainly put the inflation risk back on the radar screen," said David Gilmore, a partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics.
"I think that is dollar supportive given the interest rate implication," he added.

Trading in dollar/yen remained cautious and dealers were leery about verbal intervention on any approach of 120, especially considering recent jawboning against the strong dollar by Japanese and U.S. car makers.
U.S. officials, instead of talking it down, have recently taken to tying the strong dollar to low inflation.
Similarly,, experts said Bonn probably welcomed the strong dollar/mark as the best way to stimulate export-led growth and clear the budget deficit hurdle for currency convergence.
"I think the focus in the currency markets will shift back to what the Bundesbank is going to do with the repo rate," Gilmore said.
"It's Buba against the world. (U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert) Rubin had the opportunity yesterday to express worry about dollar gains and he didn't," Gilmore further stressed.

Broad-based mark/yen selling carried the cross down to around 63.50, from near 64.20 in early U.S. trade. Traders said bearishness is resuming and the correction from the recent low in the 62.90-area seems to be at an end.
Elsewhere, the dollar rose to 1.5245/55 Swiss from 1.5224/29 at the open and rose to Canadian $1.3784/89 from C$1.3773/78.
The pound inched up to $1.6348/58 from $1.6345/55.
((--Alden Bentley, 212 859 1667))
